Subject: VPC / On‑Prem: integration constraints and outstanding asks

Team / Kate —

Per the NDA call last week, NovaApps has a hard requirement to run a "private mode" of our inference stack inside their VPC with egress restricted, and they may move some components fully on‑prem in Q1. We need a short, concrete checklist of architecture constraints + an itemized list of asks (people + timeline) to include in the commercial proposal.

I've created an initial integration matrix (attached) where I tried to capture the minimum nets, ports, and services we would require from their side and which Redwood components could be co‑hosted vs. kept in Redwood control plane. Please review the matrix and answer the highlighted questions by EOD Monday so I can pull into the commercial working doc.

Key unknowns we need resolved:
- Can NovaApps provide a dedicated subnet with cross‑account VPC peering (or Transit Gateway)?
- Do they allow customer KMS keys in their KMS/HSM?
- Will their security team accept a managed control plane in Redwood’s VPC with a private link to their environment, or do they require full control plane handoff?
- Operational oncall model (who owns hardware incidents if on‑prem?)

Attachments: integration_matrix_v0.xlsx (sheet: constraints, sheet: service_mapping)

Short asks from us:
- Architecture answer + high‑level diagram (Karthik)
- Minimum staffing + ramp plan (Ben + Lauren)
- Security/attestation checklist we can share with NovaApps (Marissa)

Kate — if you can flag any vendor approvals or marketplace procurement constraints from your side that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Olga

Subject: Re: VPC / On‑Prem: integration constraints and outstanding asks

Thanks, Olga — reviewed the matrix and added inline comments (networking and KV cache semantics are the biggest unknowns). High‑level notes here:

1) Control plane model: we can support two options.
  - Option A (preferred): Redwood control plane in Redwood VPC + private link + service endpoints into NovaApps VPC for data plane. Lower ops for NovaApps and faster time to value.
  - Option B: Bring your own control plane (customer‑managed). Possible but requires 2–3 senior infra FTEs on their side for first 6 months to handle OS/hypervisor/patching and build the orchestration layer.

2) KV cache / stateful inference: if the model serving needs local KV (low latency) we recommend colocating serving + KV on the same hostgroup in NovaApps (or co‑located nodes in their colo). Otherwise, using a remote Redis cluster over private link adds ~6–12ms p50 to token latency depending on region.

3) Ports and NAT: we need outbound egress for telemetry and model artifact fetch (signed URLs). If egress is entirely blocked we can bake a syncer that pulls artifacts via an allowed proxy, but that adds 2–4 days to onboarding and a small ongoing maintenance delta.

See attached ops notes for cache behavior and sequence length tradeoffs.

Next steps I suggest:
- I’ll sketch a two‑panel diagram (Option A vs Option B) and a list of infra dependencies by Friday.
- Ben + Lauren: we need an initial headcount ask (SRE + Infra Eng + Solutions Eng) for Option B so sales can price appropriately.

-Karthik
